title: PESTEL Analysis
description: A PESTEL analysis is a strategic framework commonly used to evaluate the business environment in which a firm operates. Traditionally, the framework was referred to as a PEST analysis, which was an acronym for Political, Economic, Social, and Technological; in more recent history, the framework was extended to include Environmental and Legal factors as well.

title: “How to Make Great Decisions, Quickly”
description: It presents practical strategies for making good decisions quickly, including when to wait, when to act, avoiding delays due to perfectionism, etc.

title: “Data and Intuition: Good Decisions Need Both”
description: It explores the balance between decisions based on quantitative data and those that rely on intuition/experience, considering when each approach is most useful, and how to combine the two.

title: Problem Framing
description: What is problem framing, really? Problem framing is the process of discovering, analyzing, and defining the real strategic problem before committing to solutions. It connects your business objectives, customer needs, and constraints into a shared understanding of what is worth solving and why.

title: Are You Solving the Right Problem?
description: What does it take to build thought leadership that actually works in the market? This material explores problem framing, innovation inside real organizations, and why the best ideas start with solving a clear, meaningful problem. It also looks at how thought leadership grows beyond the book, turning strong concepts into practical tools, market relevance, and long-term business value.

title: Use of information sources by startup managers
description: This research focused on the use of information sources about the organizational environment by startup managers. It sought to characterize the relevance of sectors within the external environment to the business, the factors that motivate managers to seek information, and the degree of relevance and reliability of the information sources. The research methodology was based on a combination of quantitative and qualitative methods. For quantitative data collection, an online questionnaire was used, obtaining 60 responses. After analyzing the results, as a qualitative research method, interviews were conducted with three managers involved in incubation, acceleration, and investment programs for startups, so that the data could be discussed. The results demonstrated that entrepreneurs recognize customers and technology as the main sectors of the external environment affecting their businesses, and that there is a concern in seeking information to generate innovations and support decisions. Furthermore, it was possible to verify the relevance and reliability attributed to internal information sources, such as partners/employees and databases from their own companies, and the relevance of new digital information sources, to the detriment of traditional sources.

title: A systematic review of risky-choice framing effects
description: Classic decision theory requires that rational agents show description invariance: which description is chosen should not matter for judgments, preferences, or choices given the descriptions are co-extensive. Framing research has amply demonstrated a failure of description invariance by showing that the choice of the description has a systematic effect on judgments, preferences, and choices. Specifically, framing research has shown that linguistically different descriptions of seemingly equivalent options frequently lead to preference reversals.

title: How to Minimize Maximum Regret in Repeated Decision Making Decision-Making
description: This article demonstrates how simple linear strategies, requiring only one or two memory cycles, can achieve "minimax regret" in repeated decision-making processes without the use of prior environmental probabilities.

title: DECISION MAKING IN UNCERTAINTY AND RISKY ENVIRONMENT
description: This article analyzes the processes and criteria for decision-making in environments of risk and uncertainty, using a practical case study of a business affected by the Covid-19 pandemic to illustrate the application of different decision-making theories and methods.

title: DECISION MAKING IN UNCERTAINTY AND RISKY ENVIRONMENT
description: This paper explores the theoretical and practical elements of decision-making under conditions of certainty, risk, and uncertainty, applying various analytical criteria to a real-world case study of a business navigating Covid-19 pandemic restrictions

title: Decision Making Under Uncertainty
description: This chapter provides a formal, quantitative framework for decision-making under uncertainty, demonstrating how tools such as expected monetary value, decision trees, Bayes' rule, and utility functions can be used to systematically evaluate alternatives, manage risk, and optimize business strategies

title: Using a Decision Tree to help Make Decision
description: This article explains how to use a decision tree, a visual flowchart tool that helps individuals navigate complex choices by mapping out possible options, probabilities, and outcomes to calculate and compare their overall expected values

title: The Impact of Cognitive Biases on Professionals' Decision‑Making
description: This study reviews how heuristics/biases affect professional decisions in different areas: management, medicine, finance, law. It shows which biases appear, how they interfere, their limitations, etc.

title: Heuristics and Biases in Judicial Decisions
description: The text uses the metaphor of three baseball umpires to discuss the illusion of impartiality in judgments. While one recognizes his human limitations, the others assume infallibility. From this, the article shows that judges, like any person, are also subject to heuristics and cognitive biases, which function as mental shortcuts to save resources, but can generate systematic errors in decisions. These biases influence everything from the analysis of evidence to sentencing, revealing that, despite experience and training, irrelevant factors can predictably distort judgments, casting doubt on the idea of total objectivity in the judicial process.

title: The Seven Pitfalls of Data-Driven Decision-Making (And How to Avoid Them)
description: The promised powers of incorporating data into decision-making read like an advertisement: Make decisions better, faster, and more accurately! Minimize uncertainty and maximize returns! Gain agility and accountability! Facilitate innovation and disruption in all the right ways! And in reality all the hype is as advertised—when data is done right. But when data is mishandled, ignored, or even tortured, it no longer delivers the same superlative benefits.

title: Making better decisions in groups
description: This text reviews the literature to identify common problems in individual and group decision-making. Using a Bayesian framework, it explains how past experiences and new evidence interact in exploring hypotheses about different world states and possible actions. It acknowledges that biases, often unconscious, make information processing more efficient, but do not always lead to the best decision. It highlights that group decisions can help overcome these biases and broaden the search for solutions, especially when there is diversity of members. However, diverse groups also face their own challenges, requiring appropriate management strategies to improve the quality of collective decisions.

title: Decision making in the age of urgency
description: Decision making takes up a lot of time, much of it used ineffectively. New survey results offer lessons for making quick, high-quality decisions that support outperformance.

title: When Analysis Outruns Wisdom: Potential Pitfalls of Data-Driven Decision-Making
description: This article discusses potential pitfalls that can arise from data-driven decision making when not properly balanced with human judgment, strategic thinking, and organizational context. Drawing on the author's experience as a management consultant, key risks are examined such as the "tyranny of metrics" when KPIs distort goals, misinterpreting correlations as causation, overgeneralizing from limited data sets, confirmation bias within "filter bubbles," and overemphasizing quantitative data at the expense of human elements. Specific industry examples are provided to illustrate unintended consequences that have occurred. The article advocates for maintaining a multidisciplinary, questioning approach to analytics, constantly reevaluating metrics and models, supplementing internal data with external realities, and blending quantitative and qualitative inputs. Balancing these risks and enacting various safeguards can maximize the benefits of fact-based management while avoiding potential downsides.

title: Exploring top management team intuition in strategic decision-making
description: Intuition plays an essential role in strategic decision-making, helping executives navigate complex and dynamic environments. This study surveyed managers from 27 UK companies about successful and unsuccessful intuitive decisions, identifying factors that enhance or diminish the effectiveness of intuition. The results offer theoretical and practical insights into how to use intuition more effectively in the decision-making process.

title: The real power of real options
description: By applying financial options theory to strategic business investments, managers can better evaluate opportunities and proactively create value by leveraging flexibility and embracing uncertainty, which overcomes the limitations of traditional net-present-value analysis

title: Augmented analytics explained: definition, use cases, benefits, features, and more
description: Modern data is complex and sometimes difficult to interpret and understand. That’s where a tool like augmented analytics comes in handy. Harnessing machine learning and artificial intelligence to make data easier to understand is a no-brainer. But what exactly is it, and how does it work?

title: New Approaches to Project Risk Assessment Utilizing the Monte Carlo Method
description: Article published in 2023 that applies Monte Carlo simulation and sensitivity analysis to real investment-decision cases in two companies. The authors walk through the full pipeline from stochastic modeling to tornado graph, spider chart, and profit sensitivity analysis, showing how each output informs a specific part of the business recommendation. Students should focus on how the authors present results to decision-makers and on how the sensitivity analysis is used to justify the final recommendation. Direct methodological reference for the Sensitivity Analysis Report artifact.

title: Risk Taking: A Corporate Governance Perspective
description: This paper examines how organizations make decisions under uncertainty and highlights the role of governance in managing risk-taking. It presents a structured framework for decision-making that integrates tools such as scenario analysis, decision trees, and probabilistic simulations to evaluate potential outcomes and downside risks.The key takeaway is that high-quality decisions are not defined by outcomes alone, but by the robustness of the process—particularly the explicit consideration of multiple scenarios, assumptions, and risk exposures. By formalizing this process, organizations enhance transparency, improve accountability, and strengthen the defensibility of executive decisions before boards and stakeholders.

title: Strategic Intelligence: An Integrated Approach to Enterprise Risk Management
description: This article explores how organizations can enhance decision-making by integrating strategic intelligence into enterprise risk management (ERM). It emphasizes the importance of moving beyond traditional, compliance-driven risk frameworks toward a more forward-looking approach that incorporates scenario planning, stress testing, and continuous monitoring of external signals.The core idea is that organizations should actively test strategic assumptions under different scenarios, enabling leaders to anticipate potential disruptions and respond proactively. By doing so, management teams can make more resilient decisions under uncertainty, while boards gain greater visibility into key risks, underlying assumptions, and preparedness for adverse outcomes.Ultimately, the integration of strategic intelligence into ERM strengthens governance, improves the quality of strategic discussions at the board level, and supports more informed, transparent, and defensible executive decision-making.

title: AI and the future of human decision-making
description: As AI transforms decision-making, how can organizations make quality decisions, anchored in human agency and trust?

title: Artificial Intelligence + Decision-making
description: This research explores the foundations of machine learning and decision systems (artificial intelligence, reinforcement learning, statistics, causal inference, systems and control); the building blocks of embodied intelligence (computer vision, NLP, robotics); applications to real-world autonomous systems; life sciences; and the interface between data-driven decision-making and society.
